coordinates.locator: OpenStreetMap/Nominatim record of way 340213340, CERN - Point 1 (ATLAS) (reused anchor, about 480 m from the tunnel; it does not itself describe TI18)
coordinates.note: No CERN geodetic or survey publication giving WGS84 coordinates for the SND@LHC/TI18 tunnel location was found (home.cern returned 404; the INSPIRE experiment record and the collaboration's own detector paper, arXiv:2210.02784, state only the distance and direction from ATLAS IP1, not coordinates; a Nominatim/OpenStreetMap search for the tunnel name returned only generic CERN-campus results). As a placeholder, this record reuses the coordinate value already used for ATLAS Point 1 (46.2355606, 6.0546968), the nearest existing CERN point, since the detector is only about 480 m from it, well inside the stated precision. It is a campus-grade point with large uncertainty, not a surveyed hall position.

name: TI18 tunnel (SND@LHC)
notes: TI18 is a former LEP-era transfer tunnel on the opposite side of ATLAS interaction point 1 from FASER's TI12; now houses the SND@LHC detector.

The official SND@LHC site (sndlhc.web.cern.ch, sndlhc.cern, home.cern/science/experiments/snd-lhc) remains unreachable as of 2026-09-17 (DNS failure / 404, re-checked); the INSPIRE experiment record and the collaboration's own detector paper (arXiv:2210.02784) were used instead.
The coordinate is a reused neighbouring-point placeholder (campus-grade, large uncertainty); see the coordinate note.

The TI18 / 480 m siting is confirmed by the SND@LHC detector paper (arXiv:2210.02784: 'The experiment is located 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point, in the TI18 tunnel'). Only the numeric coordinate value itself remains an unverified placeholder.
country/place set to CH to match the reused anchor point (site:cern-point-1-atlas, Meyrin CH); the true tunnel geography for TI18 was not independently confirmed to finer precision.

summary.plain: An unused service tunnel at CERN, on the opposite side of the ATLAS collision point from FASER, that houses the SND@LHC experiment, which studies neutrinos and searches for rare particles produced in LHC collisions.
summary.technical: TI18, a former LEP transfer tunnel near LHC interaction point 1, on the opposite side from FASER's TI12; houses the SND@LHC detector.
